summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Addison’s disease was admitted for muscle cramps and weakness after a physically stressful week. She had self-adjusted her fludrocortisone and prednisone doses but continued to experience symptoms. Labs showed hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and metabolic acidosis consistent with acute on chronic adrenal insufficiency. She received oral hydrocortisone and IV fluids, with improvement in symptoms and electrolytes. Her prednisone was increased to 15 mg daily and fludrocortisone to 0.2 mg daily per endocrinology guidance. She remained stable, with resolving abdominal discomfort and normalized labs, and was discharged home with a steroid taper plan and follow-up scheduled.
problems: Osteoarthrosis, unspecified whether generalized or localized, site unspecified
